headline: Falling Oil Prices Cause Panic Among Petrol Pump Attendants Who Fear Their 'Price-Change' Chalkboards Will Run Out Of Eraser Dust
body:
"I just bought a premium micro-fiber duster specifically for the chalkboards, and now the prices are changing so infrequently that the dust is settling on my shoes instead of the sign," said a local petrol pump attendant who has spent the last three years perfecting his 'price-flip' speed.

"The management expects me to look busy, but when the price remains steady, I have to stand there and invent reasons for why the digits aren't moving, which is honestly more stressful than the actual inflation," remarked a neighborhood fuel kiosk operator.

"I tried to explain to my bike mechanic that the drop in prices means I can finally afford a full tank, but he told me he charges a 'Volatility Fee' for cars that don't arrive with a sense of financial urgency," noted a regular office commuter.

"My entire personality is tied to predicting whether the price will hit a new record by Friday, so this period of stability is making me feel like a retired astrologer with nothing left to forecast," claimed a local tea-stall regular.

"I used to keep a bucket of chalk by the pump just in case of a sudden shift, but now it’s just sitting there collecting cobwebs, and frankly, the lack of drama is hitting my daily adrenaline levels hard," sighed a veteran gas station supervisor.
caption: Petrol station workers are officially entering the 'Great Boredom' phase as fuel prices stabilize, leaving thousands of chalkboard-artists without a canvas. #OilPrices #PetrolPump #CommonMan #InflationStruggle (satire)
igHook: Would you miss the thrill of guessing the petrol price every time you pull up to the pump?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a dusty, faded chalkboard sign at a roadside fuel station showing numbers written in chalk, with a blurry background of a highway in the distance.
